title: Past perfect
note: had + past participle for the EARLIER of two past events. Czech has one past tense, so the Czech never picks the form - every gap carries a (lemma) cue per B11, James dropdown 2026-09-02. Scope: core sequencing + already/just/never/by the time + the over-correction guard (3 items whose answer is past simple, because Czech learners under-use this form and then over-use it) + a backshift card and three items, since the same form is what reported speech lands on (C47 shape: direct sentence, reported sentence, tense named beside each). 'd taught with the would warning - I'd + participle is had, I'd + plain verb is would (b1_used_to). Check is quiz only: a sort into earlier/later is solvable by reading 'had' off the chip, which is the B15 toll. Use is error-correction (E7); the over-correction items carry the *had made / *had walked errors. Past participle is pretaught at a2_present_perfect. Thickened 16 -> 28 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop). Rules applied this pass: A8 contraction twins closed over every accepts list; A7 everyone/someone/anyone added to the senses.json synonym map; C9 walltext cut on cards 0/1/5/6; C11 the negative and the question now have an intro card (card 4) instead of appearing only in the bank; F3 recognise swapped for a taught verb; B4/B6 the unit's own error (bare past simple, and had + past simple form) is on every option list. A4 `the` in narrative and the vocablevel candidate are queued in DECISIONS.md. A14 2026-09-04 (James smoke): every past-perfect item now carries a stated past reference point. Items 13 and 19 had a bare *before* and no anchor, so present perfect was the honest answer and 19's own Quiz offered *Have* as a distractor.

points: Both things are over. **had** marks which one happened first.

cards.title: Czech has one past tense
cards.title_cz: Čeština má jen jeden minulý čas
points: Czech uses the same past form for both events.
Nothing in the Czech says which came first. English says it with **had**.

rows: When I arrived, the film **had** started.
The train **had** left before we got there.
Nevěděl jsem, že je to ona — **ostříhala** si vlasy.
I didn't know it was her — she **had** cut her hair.

cards.title: already · just · never · by the time
cards.title_cz: already · just · never · by the time

rows: We **had already** eaten when they arrived.
He **had just** finished when I called.
**By** the time we got there, the train had left.

points: These words sit between **had** and the participle.

cards.title: When you don't need it

rows: already in order — past simple twice
She opened the door **and** walked in.
already in order — past simple twice
When I got up, my wife **had** made coffee.
out of order — the coffee came first

points: If the events are told **in order**, past simple is enough.
Use **had** when you go back to something earlier.

rows: this one is **would** — a different word

cards.title: Reporting what someone said

rows: He said he **had** seen her. *past perfect*

points: Reporting moves the verb one step back — past perfect is where it lands.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Two mistakes: leaving **had** out, and putting it in when the events are already in order.

rows: ~~When I arrived, the film already started.~~
When I arrived, the film **had** already started.
~~I couldn't get in because I lost my key.~~
I couldn't get in because I **had** lost my key.
~~I got up and had made coffee.~~

items.en: When I arrived, the film had already started.
items.cz: Když jsem přišel, film už začal.
items.gap: When I arrived, the film ____. (already / start)
accepts: When I arrived, the film had already started.
items.wrong: When I arrived, the film already started.
items.explanation: The film started **before** I arrived, so the film takes **had** + started.
items.explanation_cz: Film začal **dřív**, než jsem přišel, takže má **had** + started.

items.en: She had never seen the sea before that day.
items.cz: Do toho dne nikdy neviděla moře.
items.gap: She ____ the sea before that day. (never / see)
accepts: She had never seen the sea before that day.
She'd never seen the sea before that day.
items.wrong: She had never saw the sea before that day.
items.explanation: **never** sits between had and the participle: had **never** seen. The participle of see is **seen**.
items.explanation_cz: **never** stojí mezi had a příčestím: had **never** seen. Příčestí od see je **seen**.

items.en: I couldn't get in because I had lost my key.
items.cz: Nemohl jsem se dostat dovnitř, protože jsem ztratil klíč.
items.gap: I couldn't get in because I ____ my key. (lose)
accepts: I couldn't get in because I had lost my key.
I could not get in because I had lost my key.
I could not get in because I'd lost my key.
I couldn't get in because I'd lost my key.
items.wrong: I couldn't get in because I lost my key.
items.explanation: Losing the key happened **before** the locked door, so it takes **had** lost.
items.explanation_cz: Ztráta klíče se stala **dřív** než zamčené dveře, proto **had** lost.

items.en: By the time we got to the station, the train had left.
items.cz: Než jsme došli na nádraží, vlak odjel.
items.gap: By the time we got to the station, the train ____. (leave)
accepts: By the time we got to the station, the train had left.
items.wrong: By the time we got to the station, the train left.
items.explanation: **By the time** always looks back at something finished earlier: the train **had** left.
items.explanation_cz: **By the time** se vždycky ohlíží na něco dřívějšího: the train **had** left.

items.en: He had just finished when I called.
items.cz: Právě skončil, když jsem volal.
items.gap: He ____ when I called. (just / finish)
accepts: He had just finished when I called.
He'd just finished when I called.
items.wrong: He has just finished when I called.
items.explanation: **just** goes between had and the participle: had **just** finished. *when I called* is past, so *has* cannot stand.
items.explanation_cz: **just** patří mezi had a příčestí: had **just** finished. *when I called* je minulost, takže *has* tam nemůže být.

items.en: The room was empty. Everyone had gone home.
items.cz: Místnost byla prázdná. Všichni šli domů.
items.gap: The room was empty. Everyone ____ home. (go)
accepts: The room was empty. Everyone had gone home.
items.wrong: The room was empty. Everyone went home.
items.explanation: The empty room is the later fact; the leaving came first, so **had** gone.
items.explanation_cz: Prázdná místnost je pozdější fakt; odchod byl dřív, proto **had** gone.

items.en: I didn't know it was her because she had cut her hair.
items.cz: Nevěděl jsem, že je to ona, protože si ostříhala vlasy.
items.gap: I didn't know it was her because she ____ her hair. (cut)
accepts: I didn't know it was her because she had cut her hair.
I did not know it was her because she had cut her hair.
I did not know it was her because she'd cut her hair.
I didn't know it was her because she'd cut her hair.
items.wrong: I didn't know it was her because she cut her hair.
items.explanation: The haircut came **before** the meeting: **had** cut. The participle of cut is **cut**.
items.explanation_cz: Účes byl **dřív** než setkání: **had** cut. Příčestí od cut je **cut**.

items.en: We had already eaten when they arrived.
items.cz: Už jsme jedli, když přišli.
items.gap: We ____ when they arrived. (already / eat)
accepts: We had already eaten when they arrived.
We'd already eaten when they arrived.
items.wrong: We have already eaten when they arrived.
items.explanation: Dinner finished **before** they arrived, and *arrived* is past — so **had**, not have. Participle of eat is **eaten**.
items.explanation_cz: Večeře skončila **dřív**, než přišli, a *arrived* je minulý čas — proto **had**, ne have. Příčestí od eat je **eaten**.

items.en: I got up and made coffee.
items.cz: Vstal jsem a udělal kávu.
items.gap: I got up and ____ coffee. (make)
accepts: I got up and made coffee.
items.wrong: I got up and had made coffee.
items.explanation: These two are told **in order**, one then the other. Past simple twice — no **had** needed.
items.explanation_cz: Tyhle dvě věci jsou **v pořadí**, jedna po druhé. Dvakrát minulý čas — **had** není potřeba.

items.en: She opened the door and walked in.
items.cz: Otevřela dveře a vešla dovnitř.
items.gap: She opened the door and ____ in. (walk)
accepts: She opened the door and walked in.
items.wrong: She opened the door and had walked in.
items.explanation: Door first, then in — already **in order**, so past simple. **had** would say it happened earlier, which is false.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív dveře, pak dovnitř — už je to **v pořadí**, takže minulý čas. **had** by říkalo, že to bylo dřív, což není pravda.

items.en: I had finished my work, so I went home.
items.cz: Dodělal jsem práci, tak jsem šel domů.
items.gap: I ____ my work, so I went home. (finish)
accepts: I had finished my work, so I went home.
I'd finished my work, so I went home.
items.wrong: I have finished my work, so I went home.
items.explanation: The work finished **before** going home, and *went* is past, so **had**. Short form: **I'd** finished.
items.explanation_cz: Práce skončila **dřív** než cesta domů a *went* je minulý čas, proto **had**. Zkráceně: **I'd** finished.

items.en: By the time she called, I had gone to bed.
items.cz: Než zavolala, šel jsem spát.
items.gap: By the time she called, I ____ to bed. (go)
accepts: By the time she called, I had gone to bed.
By the time she called, I'd gone to bed.
items.wrong: By the time she called, I went to bed.
items.explanation: **By the time** she called, bed was already done: **had** gone.
items.explanation_cz: **By the time** zavolala, spaní už bylo hotové: **had** gone.

items.en: He said he had finished the report.
items.cz: Řekl, že tu zprávu dodělal.
items.gap: He said he ____ the report. (finish)
accepts: He said he had finished the report.
He said he'd finished the report.
items.wrong: He said he has finished the report.
items.explanation: Reporting his words moves the verb one step back: *I have finished* becomes he **had** finished.
items.explanation_cz: Když opakuješ jeho slova, sloveso jde o krok zpět: *I have finished* se změní na he **had** finished.

items.en: They had never been to Prague before that trip.
items.cz: Před tím výletem nikdy nebyli v Praze.
items.gap: They ____ to Prague before that trip. (never / be)
accepts: They had never been to Prague before that trip.
They'd never been to Prague before that trip.
items.explanation: **never** after had, and the participle of be is **been**. *before that trip* is the past point that makes it *had*, not *has*.
items.explanation_cz: **never** za had a příčestí od be je **been**. *before that trip* je ten bod v minulosti, proto *had*, ne *has*.

items.en: The shop was closed. It hadn't opened yet.
items.cz: Obchod byl zavřený. Ještě neotevřel.
items.gap: The shop was closed. It ____ yet. (not / open)
accepts: The shop was closed. It hadn't opened yet.
The shop was closed. It had not opened yet.
items.wrong: The shop was closed. It didn't open yet.
items.explanation: Negative: **hadn't** + opened. The closed shop is the later fact.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor: **hadn't** + opened. Zavřený obchod je pozdější fakt.

items.en: When we got home, someone had broken the window.
items.cz: Když jsme přišli domů, někdo rozbil okno.
items.gap: When we got home, someone ____ the window. (break)
accepts: When we got home, someone had broken the window.
items.wrong: When we got home, someone broke the window.
items.explanation: The window went **before** we got home. Participle of break is **broken**.
items.explanation_cz: Okno se rozbilo **dřív**, než jsme přišli. Příčestí od break je **broken**.

items.en: He had left his phone at home, so he couldn't call me.
items.cz: Nechal si telefon doma, takže mi nemohl zavolat.
items.gap: He ____ his phone at home, so he couldn't call me. (leave)
accepts: He had left his phone at home, so he couldn't call me.
He had left his phone at home, so he could not call me.
He'd left his phone at home, so he could not call me.
He'd left his phone at home, so he couldn't call me.
items.wrong: He has left his phone at home, so he couldn't call me.
items.explanation: The phone stayed at home **before** he tried to call, and *couldn't* is past — so **had** left.
items.explanation_cz: Telefon zůstal doma **dřív**, než chtěl volat, a *couldn't* je minulý čas — proto **had** left.

items.en: I couldn't pay because I had forgotten my wallet.
items.cz: Nemohl jsem zaplatit, protože jsem zapomněl peněženku.
items.gap: I couldn't pay because I ____ my wallet. (forget)
accepts: I couldn't pay because I had forgotten my wallet.
I could not pay because I had forgotten my wallet.
I could not pay because I'd forgotten my wallet.
I couldn't pay because I'd forgotten my wallet.
items.wrong: I couldn't pay because I had forgot my wallet.
items.explanation: The participle of forget is **forgotten**, not forgot: had **forgotten**.
items.explanation_cz: Příčestí od forget je **forgotten**, ne forgot: had **forgotten**.

items.en: We hadn't eaten all day, so we were very hungry.
items.cz: Celý den jsme nejedli, takže jsme měli velký hlad.
items.gap: We ____ all day, so we were very hungry. (not / eat)
accepts: We hadn't eaten all day, so we were very hungry.
We had not eaten all day, so we were very hungry.
items.wrong: We haven't eaten all day, so we were very hungry.
items.explanation: The hunger is the later fact and *were* is past, so the empty day takes **hadn't** eaten.
items.explanation_cz: Hlad je pozdější fakt a *were* je minulý čas, takže ten den bez jídla má **hadn't** eaten.

items.en: Had you ever been to London before you moved there?
items.cz: Byl jsi někdy v Londýně, než ses tam přestěhoval?
items.gap: ____ you ever been to London before you moved there? (have)
accepts: Had you ever been to London before you moved there?
items.wrong: Did you ever been to London before you moved there?
items.explanation: In a question **had** goes before the person: **Had** you been…? *before you moved* sets the past point, so *Have* is wrong here. *Did* cannot stand in front of a participle.
items.explanation_cz: V otázce jde **had** před osobu: **Had** you been…? *before you moved* určuje bod v minulosti, takže *Have* je špatně. *Did* nemůže stát před příčestím.

items.en: She said she had seen that film twice.
items.cz: Řekla, že ten film viděla dvakrát.
items.gap: She said she ____ that film twice. (see)
accepts: She said she had seen that film twice.
She said she'd seen that film twice.
items.wrong: She said she has seen that film twice.
items.explanation: *She said* is past, so what she said moves back one step: **had** seen.
items.explanation_cz: *She said* je minulý čas, takže i to, co řekla, jde o krok zpět: **had** seen.

items.en: She said she hadn't sent the email.
items.cz: Řekla, že ten e-mail neposlala.
items.gap: She said she ____ the email. (not / send)
accepts: She said she hadn't sent the email.
She said she had not sent the email.
items.wrong: She said she hasn't sent the email.
items.explanation: Her words were *I haven't sent it*; after *said* that becomes **hadn't** sent.
items.explanation_cz: Její slova byla *I haven't sent it*; po *said* se z toho stane **hadn't** sent.

items.en: After I had finished my homework, I watched television.
items.cz: Když jsem dodělal úkoly, díval jsem se na televizi.
items.gap: After I ____ my homework, I watched television. (finish)
accepts: After I had finished my homework, I watched television.
After I'd finished my homework, I watched television.
items.wrong: After I have finished my homework, I watched television.
items.explanation: **After** marks the earlier event, and *watched* is past — so the homework takes **had** finished.
items.explanation_cz: **After** označuje dřívější děj a *watched* je minulý čas — úkoly tedy mají **had** finished.

items.en: It was cold because I had opened a window.
items.cz: Byla zima, protože jsem otevřel okno.
items.gap: It was cold because I ____ a window. (open)
accepts: It was cold because I had opened a window.
It was cold because I'd opened a window.
items.wrong: It was cold because I have opened a window.
items.explanation: The window came first and *was* is past, so it takes **had** opened.
items.explanation_cz: Okno bylo dřív a *was* je minulý čas, takže má **had** opened.

items.en: I had already paid when he offered to help.
items.cz: Už jsem zaplatil, když nabídl, že pomůže.
items.gap: I ____ when he offered to help. (already / pay)
accepts: I had already paid when he offered to help.
I'd already paid when he offered to help.
items.wrong: I have already paid when he offered to help.
items.explanation: **already** sits after had, and *offered* is past — so **had already** paid.
items.explanation_cz: **already** stojí za had a *offered* je minulý čas — proto **had already** paid.

items.en: She had studied English for two years before she moved to Brno.
items.cz: Studovala angličtinu dva roky, než se přestěhovala do Brna.
items.gap: She ____ English for two years before she moved to Brno. (study)
accepts: She had studied English for two years before she moved to Brno.
She'd studied English for two years before she moved to Brno.
items.wrong: She has studied English for two years before she moved to Brno.
items.explanation: **before she moved** puts the studying earlier, and both are finished: **had** studied.
items.explanation_cz: **before she moved** klade studium dřív a obojí je uzavřené: **had** studied.

items.en: Our children had gone to bed before we got home.
items.cz: Naše děti šly spát, než jsme přišli domů.
items.gap: Our children ____ to bed before we got home. (go)
accepts: Our children had gone to bed before we got home.
items.wrong: Our children had went to bed before we got home.
items.explanation: The participle of go is **gone**, not went: had **gone**.
items.explanation_cz: Příčestí od go je **gone**, ne went: had **gone**.

items.en: He put on his coat and left.
items.cz: Oblékl si kabát a odešel.
items.gap: He put on his coat and ____. (leave)
accepts: He put on his coat and left.
items.wrong: He put on his coat and had left.
items.explanation: Coat first, then out — told **in order**, so past simple twice. **had** would put the leaving earlier, which is false.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív kabát, pak ven — je to **v pořadí**, takže dvakrát minulý čas. **had** by kladlo odchod dřív, což není pravda.
